subject: fitting binomial nonlinear model in Stan question

messages.author: ee8897fe7c1cfbec
messages.subject: fitting binomial nonlinear model in Stan question
parts:
I am trying to fit a nonlinear model in which the stochastic component is a bernoulli random variable:
     y ~ bernoulli(n, pi)

and the stochastic component is non-linear

    pi = exp(beta1*(conc - beta2)/(1 +exp(beta1*(conc - beta2) ))

The parameters being beta1 and beta2. My data looks like this:
  Obs j conc  n  y
1   1 1 50.1 48 48
2   2 2 40.7 50 47
3   3 3 30.2 49 47
4   4 4 20.4 48 34
5   5 5 10.0 48 18
6   6 6  5.1 49 16


 I am struggling to fit this model in Stan. Here's my attempt:

model<-"data {
int<lower=0> N;
vector[N] y;
vector[N] conc;
vector[N] n;
}
parameters {
vector[2] beta;
real<lower=0, upper=1> pi;
}
model {
y ~ binomial(n, pi);
pi <- exp(beta[1]*(conc - beta[2])/(1 +exp(beta[1]*(conc - beta[2]) ));
}"


d_stan <- list(
  N = nrow(d),
  y = d$y,
  conc = d$conc,
  n = d$n)

fit <- stan(model_code = model, data = d_stan,
            iter = 1000, chains = 4)

Stan throws an error indicating: 
No matches for: 

  vector ~ binomial(vector, real)

I am unsure how to rectify the model statement. Any help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: fitting binomial nonlinear model in Stan question
parts:
Several things here:

(1) y and n should be declared as integer array and not vectors (which contain real numbers). So you need int y[N] and likewise for n.

(2) pi should be declared in the transformed parameters block since it is a deterministic function of parameters. It also needs to have N elements, one for each value of conc. The statement assigning a value to pi that you have in the model block also should move to transformed parameters as a loop (I don't think exp is vectorized yet, but I might be wrong).

That should get the model running. However, you can and should avoid all of (2) by using y~binomial_logit(n, beta[1]*(conc - beta[2])), which does it all on the logit scale for you so you don't need to do the transformation yourself.

I hope that helps. If any of that doesn't make sense let me know.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: fitting binomial nonlinear model in Stan question
parts: There's also an inverse logit function (inv_logit) which you can use instead of doing all the exping yourself. But the recommended way is to just use binomial_logit so that you get to work on the linear scale and Stan takes care of the nonlinear transformation for you (with greater numerical stability too).

> pi <- exp(beta[1]*(conc - beta[2])/(1 +exp(beta[1]*(conc - beta[2]) ));

1. You can't assign to parameters like pi, so it needs to be a local.

2. You need to define pi before you use it.

3. But you don't need any of that in Stan.

4. y needs to be declared as an array of integers because binomials
use count data and vectors are continuous data by definition in Stan.
I don't know if n is count, too, in which case it should also be an integer.

data {
int y[N];
...
parameters {
vector[2] beta;
}
model {
real pi;

y ~ binomial(n, pi);

beta ~ ???
}

5. You probably want some kind of prior on beta. It's not necessary if
the posterior's proper, but it's usually a good idea.

- Bob
